title: DashboardPipeline
wrapsNative: MonarchDashboardGrid (androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.grid.LazyVerticalGrid) of a MonarchStatCard row (androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow), MonarchFunnelChart, a MonarchSectionCard of MonarchCheckboxRow tasks (the TodayPanel recipe), MonarchLeaderboard in a MonarchWidget and MonarchActivityTimeline
summary: The home screen of a pipeline product (sales, hiring, campaigns): key figures, items by stage, today's tasks, top performers and recent activity, as sections of a MonarchDashboardGrid.
whenToUse: As the home screen of a sales, hiring, campaign or deal product, whose main question is what is moving and what is waiting on me.
whenNotToUse: For live operational work (incidents, tickets) use the DashboardOperational recipe; for a set of owned assets use DashboardPortfolio; for a person's own task list use DashboardPersonalWork.
api: MonarchDashboardGrid(items = sections, key = { it }, itemLabel = { it }, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize(), span = { … }) { section -> when (section) { "Key figures" -> FlowRow(maxItemsInEachRow = 2) { MonarchStatCard(…) }; "Pipeline" -> MonarchFunnelChart(title = …, stages = …); "Today" -> MonarchSectionCard(title = "Today", meta = date) { MonarchCheckboxRow(…) }; "Top performers" -> MonarchWidget(title = …) { MonarchLeaderboard(entries = …) }; else -> MonarchWidget(title = "Recent activity") { MonarchActivityTimeline(…) } } }

options.name: sections
options.description: The sections in order; leave out what the product has no data for. The web's slots are pipeline, today, followUps, upcoming, performance, leaders and activity.

options.name: key figures
options.description: The KPI row, as the first full-span item (the KpiRow recipe).

options.name: pipeline
options.description: Items by stage with the step rates; a MonarchBarList also works for stages that are not a funnel.

options.name: today
options.description: Today's tasks and meetings (the TodayPanel recipe).

options.name: waiting on you / coming up / performance
options.description: Short lists or a chart, linking to the full view with View all.

options.name: leaders
options.description: Top performers, with highlightTop for the first three.

states.name: loading or failed section
states.description: MonarchWidget with state = Loading or Failed and onRetry, MonarchStatCard with loading, or the chart's status, per section.

states.name: editing
states.description: MonarchDashboardGrid with editing = true shows arrange bars to move sections, with TalkBack actions.

appearance: Widgets, section cards and stat cards on the surface color with the subtle border; the funnel and leaderboard bars in the data colors; checkboxes and badges in the Monarch theme. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web DashboardPipeline is one template with a header, a KPI row, an insight strip and named slots (with a built-in TodayPanel) in a responsive grid. On Android it is a recipe the app owns: MonarchDashboardGrid is the screen's scrolling list (one column on a phone, more from 1024dp, rearrangeable with editing), and each section is a Monarch part. The title, period and actions belong to the screen's TopAppBar. Lazy parts such as MonarchActivityTimeline or a MonarchAgendaList in Today get a bounded height inside a grid item. Section structure (C-050, aligned with the iOS recipe): the same sections in the same order as the web template and iOS: a summary line, the key figures (four stat cards), the insight strip, then Pipeline (the funnel chart itself), Today (event chips in a widget, as in the today-panel recipe), Waiting on you, Coming up, Performance (a bar list), Top performers and Recent activity, with Pipeline and Performance two columns wide on a tablet. Remaining differences from iOS: the summary, key figures and insights are the first full-width items of MonarchDashboardGrid, because on Android the grid is the screen's one scrolling list; the title, period and primary action go to the TopAppBar; the leaderboard writes its own short currency values (display) where iOS formats them with a currency format.
accessibility: Each widget's and section card's title is a heading, and the key figures are one traversal group named after the section.
The funnel chart reads each stage with its value and step rate and has a table view.
Today's tasks are checkbox rows: one TalkBack element each with the checkbox role and state.
Rearranging sections has TalkBack custom actions in MonarchDashboardGrid, so dragging is never required.
edgeCases: Keep each section short and link to the full view with View all.
A lazy timeline or agenda inside a grid item needs a bounded height.
Never put the grid inside a vertically scrolling parent; it is the screen's list.
